subject: Discovery recap: BrightCart embeddings & reranking
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, dev.patel@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 24 Feb 2026 11:00:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery recap: BrightCart \u2014 embeddings & reranking

Hi Jenna / Marco,

Appreciate your time today. Below is a quick recap of our discussion and proposed next steps so we're aligned heading into the pilot. Please flag any gaps or corrections.

High-level pain and goals
- Current keyword-based search surface is returning irrelevant or stale items; conversion from search-driven product discovery is ~40% below site average.
- Goal: improve ranking relevance for search/results recommendations and drive measurable uplift in conversion.
- Success metrics for pilot: improve top-10 relevance leading to +8-12% conversion lift on search-driven flows; maintain end-to-end p95 latency <150ms (target p50 <=75ms if achievable).

Current stack (as discussed)
- Catalog: ~12M SKUs today (~75M variant records including images and metadata).
- Embeddings: in-house 768-d embeddings produced via PyTorch pipeline; nightly full-batch + streaming incremental updates.
- Indexing & retrieval: FAISS with S3 snapshot backups; small PoC leveraging Pinecone for specific projects.
- Reranking: existing approach is heuristics + sparse features; exploring replacing top-50 scoring with a lightweight neural reranker.

Workload specifics you shared
- Index scale: 12M active vectors now, expected to grow to ~18-20M within 9 months.
- Embedding throughput: nightly batches ~50k items/day, near-real-time updates 3-5k/day.
- Traffic: baseline retrieval QPS ~80 with spikes to ~400 during peaks.
- Latency & cost targets: ideal p50 end-to-end 50-100ms, p95 <150ms; pilot cost target <$0.01/query (goal long-term <$0.005).

Proposed pilot scope (recommended)
- Objective: validate an LLM-based reranker + Redwood-managed retrieval path on a 2M-product subset to measure relevance improvement, latency, and per-query cost.
- Deliverables: 1) 2M subset ingest and indexing, 2) A/B evaluation results vs baseline heuristics, 3) latency/cost report and recommended production config (sharding/quantization/batching).
- Timeline: ~6 weeks to complete pilot (ingest, run experiments, deliver report).

Open questions to confirm
- Any additional compliance/data residency constraints (KMS/HSM, SOC2 evidence) beyond what we covered?
- Is the intent to keep FAISS as primary infra with Pinecone for short-term PoC, or move to a managed vector DB longer-term?
- Which exact SLIs and dashboards should we target for pilot measurement (conversion lift, CTR, p50/p95 latency broken out by retrieval vs rerank)?

Next steps
1) I'll email a short pilot SOW + milestone plan by EOD tomorrow.
2) Rishi will prepare two infra + cost options for the pilot (Managed vs Hybrid).
3) Dev will estimate engineering effort for ingestion & near-real-time updates for the 2M subset.
4) Schedule technical deep-dive next week (Tue/Thu afternoon PST).

Attachments: discovery notes (PDF), proposed pilot scope (XLSX).

Thanks again \u2014 looking forward to the next steps.

Thanks Marissa \u2014 this summary looks good and captures the call. A couple clarifications from our side:

- Latency: SRE would like p50 <= 75ms if possible for the production rerank path. p95 <150ms is acceptable for the pilot, but p50 is important for UX.
- Index growth: 12M active today; plan for 18-20M within 9 months due to seasonal catalog additions.
- Vector DB: We have an active paid PoC with Pinecone but want to avoid lock-in \u2014 leaning toward a hybrid approach long-term (managed + FAISS).
- Pilot budget: We have up to $35k discretionary for engineering + cloud for the POC.

Stakeholders to include on technical deep-dive: Marco (CTO) and Lina Chavez (Head of Search, lina.chavez@brightcart.com). I'll loop Lina once we confirm a time.

We're available Tue/Thu afternoons PST for the deep-dive.

Thanks,
